title: Here’s Exactly How Tesla Made Its New 230-Mph Car ‘Fly’
gist: Tesla unveiled the Roadster 2 with a stunt using suction fans and cold-gas nitrogen thrusters; WIRED details the specs and a 2028 production timeline, noting past delays and that Tesla stock fell after the event.

insights.claim: Roadster 2 is rear-wheel-drive only with two motors delivering over 1 MW (1,341 hp) and over 1,400 Nm of torque, at just under 1,700 kg.
insights.speaker: Jeremy White
insights.so_what: Specs headline the halo product but are Tesla-supplied claims.

insights.claim: Tesla claims a range over 300 miles and a battery that charges from 15 to 80 percent in 10 minutes, its fastest-charging yet.
insights.speaker: Jeremy White
insights.so_what: Fast-charging claim is unverified and relevant to Tesla battery roadmap.
insights.locator: Tesla claims a range of over 300 miles

insights.claim: Four 20-kW fans and drop-down skirts form a 'sucker system' that Tesla says produces over 2 g in corners below 50 mph.
insights.speaker: Jeremy White
insights.so_what: Active-downforce tech borrowed from niche hypercars.

insights.claim: A 'SpaceX system' of cold gas nitrogen thrusters, fed by a 200-liter 10,000 PSI vessel, yields over 80 kN of thrust in launch mode and 0-60 mph in under a second, versus 1.6 seconds for the thruster-less Performance model.
insights.speaker: Jeremy White
insights.so_what: Performance tiering: only the Thrust variant gets the full package.

insights.claim: The 'flight system' needs another 400-liter tank and six more thrusters, and thrust fades as gas depletes, like a balloon deflating; refilling takes six to seven hours, with Tesla working on 30 minutes.
insights.speaker: Jeremy White
insights.so_what: The flying demo is far from a practical product.

insights.claim: Production is not expected until 2028 although Musk previously promised Roadster deliveries in 2020, and the FAA's reaction to a 'flying' car is unknown.
insights.speaker: Jeremy White
insights.so_what: Long delay history argues for discounting Tesla timelines.
insights.quote: take this with a very large pinch of salt

insights.claim: Reservations are open: $5,000 down plus $45,000 within 10 days for the Performance, and $5,000 plus $245,000 for the Thrust model; Tesla stock was down after the event.
insights.speaker: Jeremy White
insights.so_what: Pricing implies about $50,000 and $250,000 commitments and a market not impressed by the spectacle.
